description: Numbered-Pinyin -> diacritic-form test table for the stage-7 conversion function (data-pipeline.md §3). Authored by Red (WO-006). This is the authority Black's implementation is checked against, and the fixture set for the build-time round-trip gate (testing-strategy.md §3.1). Rule numbers in each row's "rule" field refer to data-pipeline.md §3's numbered list.

conventions.u_colon_to_umlaut: CC-CEDICT encodes ü as the two-character sequence 'u:' immediately followed by the tone digit, e.g. 'lu:4'. Rule 1 replaces 'u:' with 'ü' before any tone-mark placement logic runs. See group A.
conventions.jqxy_u_convention: CONFIRMED: after the initials j, q, x, and y, CC-CEDICT writes a bare 'u' with no colon, because the vowel is unambiguously ü in that phonological position (standard Mandarin has no j/q/x/y + true-u syllable). The diacritic output for these syllables therefore takes a PLAIN u-with-tone-mark (ū/ú/ǔ/ù), never the umlaut form (ǖ/ǘ/ǚ/ǜ) — e.g. 'qu4' -> 'qù', not 'qǜ'. The converter must not apply any ü-substitution to a bare 'u' in this position; there is nothing to substitute, since no colon is present. See group B.
conventions.erhua: The r5 suffix (rule 8) FUSES directly onto the end of the preceding syllable's diacritic form with no space and contributes no tone mark of its own — 'yi1 hui4 r5' -> 'yī huìr', not 'yī huì r'. This is standard Pinyin orthographic practice (the -r suffix is never set off by a space) and takes precedence over the general space-joining rule (rule 7), which applies to ordinary syllable-to-syllable joins only. A standalone 儿 word (reading er2, meaning 'son/child') is a complete syllable in its own right and is NOT the same case: it takes its own full tone mark and, in a multi-syllable word, its own space, exactly like any other syllable. See group C.
conventions.neutral_tone: Tone digit 5 produces no mark. CC-CEDICT's own data always supplies an explicit digit 1-5 for every syllable, including neutral tone as '5' — a bare no-digit syllable does not occur in CC-CEDICT itself. Rule 2's parenthetical '(or no digit)' is nonetheless tested here defensively (case neutral-2) so the converter's behaviour is pinned for a bare-syllable input too, since the function may see reuse beyond this corpus; both forms must produce no mark.
conventions.capitalization: CC-CEDICT capitalises only the first letter of the first syllable of a proper noun or surname reading; subsequent syllables in the same word stay lowercase even though they are part of the same proper name — e.g. 'Zhong1 guo2' (not 'Zhong1 Guo2'), 'Bei3 jing1'. This must be preserved verbatim through the conversion (rule 6), including inside a longer word where the proper noun is only the first component (see 'Zhong1 guo2 ren2' in group K).
